主要内容: The U.S. Department of the Treasury announced a $120 billion issuance of Treasury securities to refund $75.9 billion in privately-held notes and bonds maturing on November 15, 2021. This will raise approximately $44.1 billion in new cash. The securities include a $56 billion 3-year note, a $39 billion 10-year note, and a $25 billion 30-year bond, all maturing on November 15, 2024, 2031, and 2051, respectively. Auctions for these securities will occur on November 8, 9, and 10, 2021, with settlements on November 15, 2021. The Treasury also plans to reduce auction sizes for various securities over the next quarter to preserve flexibility in financing plans. These changes will be announced quarterly in subsequent refunding statements. The U.S. Department of the Treasury announced a quarterly refunding statement on November 3, 2021, detailing changes in auction sizes for various securities. The reductions in auction sizes for 7-year and 20-year coupon securities reflect the Treasury's effort to balance structural supply and demand at these tenors. These tenors saw significant increases in borrowing needs due to the COVID-19 pandemic, and the reduction of supply at these tenors has been a focus of market feedback. The table outlines the anticipated auction sizes for the November 2021 through January 2022 quarter, showing a $84 billion reduction in issuance to private investors compared to the August–October 2021 quarter. The Treasury also announced plans to maintain TIPS auction sizes, with a $17 billion increase in total gross issuance of TIPS in CY 2021 compared to CY 2020. Additionally, the Treasury stated that an FRN linked to the Secured Overnight Financing Rate (SOFR) is not necessary at this time. The debt limit was increased by $480 billion on October 14, 2021, and the Treasury has been using extraordinary measures to finance the government temporarily.
